messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate (threshold 7% over 2m) observed for LumosCorp private VPC (vpc-lumos-prod). Path: /inference/generate. Egress NLB: nlb-lumos-egress-01. Please `ack` to claim.

oncall-liz: ack. I'm on it. paging @sre-rob @netops-maya @eng-runtime-arya. Lumos customer-eng on standby.

sre-rob: starting triage. checking NLB target health and ALB. @netops-maya can you paste NLB target statuses?

netops-maya: NLB targets for blue pool showing intermittent Unhealthy -> Healthy flips. CloudWatch shows increased TCP_Rst and ELB_5XX at 03:10 UTC for az-a targets. ALB `alb-private-01` reports 503s from backend.

eng-runtime-arya: runtime metrics show a spike in upstream connection resets and TLS handshake failures when egressing to customer proxy (10.3.2.18:443). stack shows lots of SYNs then RST mid-handshake.

customer-eng-jensen: Lumos noticing failed requests and slow responses. They report client-side timeouts and are asking for ETA.

oncall-liz: immediate plan: 1) move new traffic off blue pool (drain), 2) shift Route53 internal weight to green if healthy, 3) check for recent SG or automation changes. rob proceed with draining. maya check NAT/conntrack.

sre-rob: running drain cmd on blue target group, deregistration-delay=0. `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:tg-blue --targets Id=...` Monitoring target health.

netops-maya: saw a failed SG prune automation job at 03:08 UTC. The job logged an incomplete rollback and left iptables rules on the NAT instance that limited ephemeral port ranges for outbound. NAT instance conntrack table at ~78% capacity. That would cause new TCP sessions to be dropped mid-handshake.

eng-runtime-arya: that matches the TLS handshake aborts. If NAT conntrack saturated, we'll get connection resets. We should flush conntrack after we remove blue from rotation to avoid flapping when green takes on traffic.

oncall-liz: rob -> finish cutover to green if healthy. maya -> try conntrack flush or scale NAT. Also confirm whether this is BYO NAT instance or managed NAT Gateway.

netops-maya: Lumos uses a BYO NAT instance (nat-lumos-01). I'm ssh-ing to bastion -> then NAT. Running `sudo conntrack -L | wc -l` -> ~780k entries. Flushing now: `sudo conntrack -F`. After flush, count drops to ~12k.

sre-rob: blue targets drained. updated Route53 internal record weights (blue:0 green:100). TTL 20s. green targets showing healthy.

prod-ops-bot: autopilot: runtime canary rollback triggered due to health anomalies: rollback v2.9.1 -> v2.8.7 started.

eng-runtime-arya: keepalive tweak applied to runtime (temporary): `keepalive: enabled` to reduce handshake churn. Also watching error rate.

metrics-watch: 5xx rate fell from 8.6% -> 1.0% over 90s after drain + conntrack flush.

se-cs-ivana: drafting customer-facing note: "We identified a transient outbound connection resource saturation on the customer's NAT instance caused by an incomplete automation rollback. We drained the affected backend pool, flushed NAT conntrack, and rolled back a runtime canary. Service has been restored. No customer action required. Full postmortem and RCA to follow." Thoughts?

customer-eng-jensen: Lumos responded: thanks, please include action items and ETA for permanent fix. They asked if any IP allowlist changes were part of this (they said they didn't change anything).

netops-maya: SG audit: no manual SG edits from Lumos or our team. The automation job is the likely culprit. Automation logs:
```
2026-03-15T03:08:12Z sg-pruner ERROR Failed to apply pruned ruleset; rollback incomplete
stack: ...
```

infra-oliver: adding infra note: we should consider replacing BYO NAT instance with AWS-managed NAT Gateway for this tenant to avoid single-instance conntrack limits. I'll open infra ticket.

oncall-liz: good. Rob/Maya prepare handoff doc for followup at 10:30 PDT and owners for postmortem.

sre-rob: timeline draft to attach to incident ticket RDW-INC-2201:
- 03:07 UTC alert: 5xx spike
- 03:08 UTC automation job sg-pruner failed
- 03:09 UTC NAT conntrack ~78% (nat-lumos-01)
- 03:11 UTC conntrack flushed
- 03:12 UTC blue target group deregistered; Route53 weight -> green
- 03:13 UTC runtime canary rollback started
- 03:15 UTC 5xx rate < threshold

se-cs-ivana: customer blurb ready. adding SLA credit request instructions for product/legal if needed.

netops-maya: follow-ups:
- fix sg-pruner automation race and add unit/integration tests (PR #1234)
- add conntrack high-water alert and automated mitigation (flush or scale)
- evaluate BYO NAT -> managed NAT Gateway migration for Lumos
- harden ephemeral port handling and raise ip_conntrack_max on NAT instance

eng-runtime-arya: follow-ups from runtime side: add circuit breaker to avoid repeating connections to failing upstreams, keepalive and connection pooling improvements (tracked in RFC).

sre-rob: opening Jira RDW-INC-2201 and uploading NLB/ALB CloudWatch logs and conntrack dump to `s3://redwood-incidents/lumos/1778880660/`.

prod-ops-bot: reminder: run `incident close` when done and tag severity.

oncall-liz: marking mitigated at 03:15 UTC. We'll monitor for 2 hours. Owners: @sre-rob (follow-ups + Jira), @netops-maya (automation + NAT plan), @infra-oliver (infra migration evaluation), @eng-runtime-arya (runtime fixes). Thanks team :thumbsup:

customer-eng-jensen: Lumos confirms traffic normal again. They'll schedule a follow-up with our PMs about NAT migration and SLA credits.

eng-runtime-arya: paste relevant log snippet for postmortem:
```
2026-03-15T03:10:50Z runtime error: dial tcp 10.3.2.18:443: connect: connection reset by peer
2026-03-15T03:11:12Z runtime: retry 1
2026-03-15T03:11:42Z net: conntrack entries 780321/1_000_000
```

netops-maya: automation stacktrace:
```
2026-03-15T03:08:12Z sg-pruner ERROR Failed to apply new ruleset; rollback incomplete
Trace: ...
```

oncall-liz: links: runbook -> https://runbooks.redwood.internal/networking/nat-conntrack ; incident -> https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RDW-INC-2201

sre-rob: final: incident mitigated. severity S2. duration ~8 minutes from alert to mitigation. Postmortem owners assigned. I'll schedule internal review with Lumos next week."
